summary: A notice cancelling the Resource Notebook Framework meeting that had tentatively been set for March 19, 1973, with more information on the framework from RFC 464 promised soon. It lists the NIC contacts for questions.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC cancels a planned Resource Notebook Framework meeting. It says more information would follow and gives contacts for questions.

subtitle: Cancellation of the Resource Notebook Framework meeting.

tldr.problem: A Resource Notebook Framework meeting had been tentatively scheduled for March 19, 1973.
tldr.mechanism: The NIC announced that the meeting was cancelled and referred readers to RFC 464 for background.
tldr.outcome: The notice says further information would be distributed soon and provides NIC contacts for questions.

today: The unit metadata lists RFC 483's status as Unknown. The RFC records cancellation of a planned meeting.

sections.title: The Meeting Is Cancelled
sections.content: RFC 483 announces that the Resource Notebook Framework meeting tentatively scheduled for March 19, 1973, is cancelled. The notice refers readers to RFC 464 for background.
sections.plainLanguage: The meeting planned for March 19 was cancelled. The notice points readers to RFC 464 for background.

sections.title: Further Information and Contacts
sections.content: The RFC says further information about the framework discussed in RFC 464 would be distributed soon. It asks people with questions to contact Jake Feinler or Mike Kudlick at the NIC.
sections.plainLanguage: The NIC said it would share more information later. Jake Feinler or Mike Kudlick could answer questions.

sections.title: Scope of the Notice
sections.content: This brief RFC gives the cancellation, a reference for background, and contact information. It does not describe the Resource Notebook Framework itself.
sections.plainLanguage: This RFC is an administrative notice, not a description of the framework. It gives only the meeting update and contact details.

references.text: Bressler, B., "Resource Notebook Framework Proposal", RFC 464, March 1973.
